title: Product capability showcase (docs/capabilities.json)
$comment: The family capability-showcase contract (plan 43). One per product repo, at docs/capabilities.json: WHAT THE PRODUCT CAN DO, codified so the hub site can render it (compact strip, detail view, capability page) and every agent that ships a feature updates it in the same change. v1.3 (plan 46) removed the family matrix and the preview-widget hints. v1.4 (plan 47) removed `shot`: the hub shows product captures on ONE surface only (the visual tour) — repeating them in feature rows and capability pages read as filler. NOT the extension-manifest `capabilities` flags (net/sync/…, extension-manifest.schema.json) and NOT the capability RPC (capability-rpc.schema.json) — those describe extension runtime surface; this file describes product-level user-facing capabilities. Discipline mirrors docs-tree.schema.json: draft 2020-12, only the keyword subset scripts/lib/docs-tree-validate.mjs implements, closed vocabularies as enums with $comment rationales, additionalProperties:false everywhere. Content is verifiable FACTS + short English labels (plan 43 §1.4): persuasion copy lives on the website; per-locale prose rides the optional i18n map. A field that cannot be verified does not belong here.

version.$comment: Contract version. Bumping is a family decision (the family product-capabilities contract first, re-vendor everywhere).

project.$comment: Must match the product repo it lives in — the hub's sync cross-checks it against the manifest slug.

updated.$comment: ISO date the capability list was last REVIEWED against the shipped product (content date, hand-maintained — never the sync date).

useCases.$comment: Concrete scenarios a visitor recognizes themselves in ('Compare cholesterol across two labs after switching providers — …'), verb-first, one per line. Optional; when present the hub renders them as the 'what you can do with it' section on the capability page. These are REPRESENTATIVE, not exhaustive — pick the five that best say what the product is for.

projectSlug.$comment: Closed family roster. A new product ADDS a slug here (canonical-first + re-vendor) — it never forks the vocabulary. Mirrors src/data/projects.ts on the hub.

id.$comment: Stable kebab-case slug. It is the anchor (#cap-<id>), the i18n key and the deep-link target — once shipped, an id is renamed only with a redirect note, never reused for a different capability.

verb.$comment: Verb-first, present tense, user's outcome ('Catch dangerous interactions') — NOT a feature name ('Interaction checker'). This is the first-minute line; it must read standalone.

summary.$comment: One sentence, how it works for the user. Facts only — no marketing adjectives, no superlatives.

category.$comment: Closed grouping vocabulary for the detail view and filter chips. discover = find/explore things; analyze = insights, charts, understanding; automate = flows, background jobs, shortcuts; integrate = connectors, import/export, extensions; ai = chat/LLM-powered; privacy = local-first, security, data control; developer = SDK/API/scripting. A capability that fits none of these EXTENDS this enum (family decision, canonical-first).

audience.$comment: Mirrors the docs.md audience split, closed. Absent = 'user'.

status.$comment: Closed lifecycle. Only 'shipped' capabilities may claim metrics/proofs; 'planned' ones render dimmed and must not be counted in the headline strip. (A structure gate is not a truth gate — pin the semantics repo-side.)

proof.$comment: One verifiable statement ('Runs fully offline — nothing leaves the device'). Claims like 'best' or 'blazing fast' fail the spirit of this contract even though the schema cannot smell them.

metricValue.$comment: The number itself, verbatim ('2s', '40+', '100%'). No units prose — units go in metric.label.

metric.$comment: At most one proof number per capability, shown as a chip. Absent = no chip (never invent a metric to fill the slot).

linkKind.$comment: Closed door vocabulary. 'guide'/'api' hrefs point at hub docs routes or upstream docs; 'source' at the repository. The hub maps unknown-to-it targets through the same tolerant rules as extension links — a link that cannot resolve is a gate failure, never a dead door.

href.$comment: Two shapes only: an absolute https:// URL (repo, product site, demo), or a locale-less HUB DOCS ROUTE 'docs/<project>/<audience>/<slug>' resolved against the hub's vendored docs at render time. No http:// (CSP forbids external non-https origins), no free-form relative paths — a href that cannot resolve is a gate failure, never a dead door.

label.$comment: Optional display override; absent = the kind's i18n label on the hub.

platform.$comment: Mirrors the hub's PlatformIcon vocabulary (src/data/projects.ts), closed. Where the capability actually runs — not the product's whole platform list.

localeCode.$comment: BCP-47-ish, mirrors the hub locale codes (en, el, de, es, fr, pt-BR, it, pl, tr).

proofs.$comment: When present, replaces the English proofs 1:1 (same length, same order).

capStrings.$comment: Per-locale override of the English strings. Absent locales fall back to the English fields (graceful degradation — the hub renders English until a translation lands).

order.$comment: Sort weight, ascending; ties break on id. The FIRST-MINUTE STRIP takes the lowest-order shipped capabilities (the hub asks for 3). Write them in the order you would tell a new user about them.

visual.$comment: Optional component capture (alpha) shown floating in the feature row. One per capability — it appears exactly once on the whole site.

visualPath.$comment: COMPONENT CAPTURE: the capability's UI element ISOLATED as it really renders (element crop, never the page — no window chrome, no desktop). PNG or WebP, ~2x density, 480–900 px on the long edge, named after the capability id, path relative to this manifest (docs/images/components/<id>.png). Produced by the product's own capture pipeline; scenes with `tour: false` + `capture: "element"` write it (guidelines/component-captures.md). Transparency is optional: floating components capture with alpha (rendered with a drop-shadow), surfaced cards keep their own surface (rendered as a framed card). Rendered ONCE, in the project page feature rows.
